ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Ida B. Wells

code.originalText: Four weeks after starting dapagliflozin: potassium, creatinine and blood pressure, the losartan dose, and the plan for the months ahead

text.paragraph: Four weeks after starting dapagliflozin: potassium, creatinine and blood pressure, the losartan dose, and the plan for the months ahead. [S]

Mrs. Wells returns two weeks after her annual wellness visit and four weeks after starting dapagliflozin. She has had no dizziness, genital itching or sick days. Her home readings average 130/78. Her ankles have not swollen for three weeks and her afternoons are easier, though she still tires on long writing days. Since the kidney education session she has written down her questions about transplant evaluation for her next nephrology visit. She asked for the COVID-19 vaccine today. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-03-03; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 132/80, pulse 72; weight 68.9 kg

Tiredness for some months and ankle swelling by evening, with a raised creatinine (1.42 mg/dL, race-free eGFR 40, confirmed at 38 with cystatin C) and albumin in the urine (240 mg/g) found today; cause and chronicity to be established
S — Synthetic presenting finding, superseded by the kidney diagnosis at two weeks.
Elevated blood pressure at intake (164/94 mmHg, average of two readings), without a diagnosis of hypertension; home readings for one week to confirm
S — Synthetic presenting finding, superseded by the confirmed diagnosis at two weeks.
Hypertension, stage 2, confirmed by home readings (average 150/88 mmHg), with chronic kidney disease
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; no blood pressure from her life is recorded.

Chronic kidney disease G3b A2 (eGFR 38 by creatinine and cystatin C, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 240 and 228 mg/g), present at least two years; small, echogenic kidneys without obstruction; most likely hypertensive kidney disease, with APOL1-associated disease possible; 5-year kidney failure risk about 7%
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis linked to the kidney disease recorded at her death.
Anemia of chronic kidney disease, mild (hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL) with adequate iron stores; a likely part of her tiredness
Vitamin D deficiency (25-hydroxyvitamin D 17 ng/mL) with a mildly raised PTH (84 pg/mL); calcium and phosphate normal
S — Synthetic laboratory finding, part of the mineral and bone check in kidney disease.

list.item: Blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg in the clinic and at home within two months of starting treatment, and lower if tolerated. Outcome by 2026-03-03: 132/80 in the clinic and 130/78 at home on losartan 50 mg and dapagliflozin; losartan increased to 100 mg [S]
Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio lower by at least 30% at the three-month check on treatment. Outcome by 2026-03-03: 240 and 228 mg/g at baseline; repeat due at three months on treatment [S]

No NSAIDs or other avoidable kidney harms; every medicine checked against her kidney function. Outcome by 2026-03-03: Naproxen stopped at intake; acetaminophen used instead; medicines checked at every visit [S]
An informed decision about APOL1 genetic testing, made by her after counseling. Outcome by 2026-01-20: Counseled at the consultation; she chose to defer the test and may ask for it at any time [S]

She understands her stage, her risk and the kidney replacement options, and her wishes are recorded, long before any decision is needed. Outcome by 2026-02-17: Kidney education session completed; wishes recorded at the annual wellness visit [S]

Follow-up: Potassium and creatinine in two to four weeks. Review with the urine albumin, hemoglobin, PTH and vitamin D in three months, and nephrology review then. Call for dizziness, vomiting or diarrhea (hold losartan and dapagliflozin that day), or swelling of the lips or tongue (call 911). [S]
